turns.responseText:
IVIVE Hepatic Clearance — Scales in vitro microsomal CLint to predicted human hepatic clearance and extraction ratio for 4 BCR-ABL1 TKIs using well-stirred and parallel-tube models.

Input: Compound data CSV with 4 BCR-ABL1 TKIs (compound_id, CLint_uL_per_min_mg, molecular_weight columns)
Key steps:

CLint scaling → PKNCA/IVIVE engine applies microsomal protein binding corrections and liver microsomal scaling factors (MPPGL) to compute intrinsic clearance per compound
Well-stirred + parallel-tube models → predicted human CLh (mL/min/kg) and hepatic extraction ratio (EH) per TKI


Expected output: ivive_results.csv (CLh and EH per compound) + clearance_summary.json (model comparison, scaling assumptions, fu,mic corrections)

Decision gate: Flag any compound with EH > 0.7 as high-extraction (first-pass effect risk, high sensitivity to hepatic blood flow changes) and EH < 0.3 as low-extraction (sensitive to fu,p and CLint changes — prioritize for plasma protein binding assays).

IVIVE Hepatic Clearance — BCR-ABL1 TKI Panel — Scales in vitro microsomal CLint to predicted human hepatic clearance (CLh) and extraction ratio (EH) for 4 BCR-ABL1 TKIs using the well-stirred liver model.

Input: bcr_abl1_tki_ivive_input.csv (generated above) — 4 compounds (Dasatinib, Bosutinib, Imatinib, Nilotinib) with CLint, fu_plasma, fu_mic=1.0; model parameters: Qh=20.7 mL/min/kg, well-stirred model selected
Key steps:

CLint scaling → IVIVE engine applies MPPGL (microsomal protein per gram liver) and liver weight scaling to convert μL/min/mg → CLint,scaled (mL/min/kg); fu_mic correction applied per compound
Well-stirred model → CLh = Qh × (fu_plasma × CLint,scaled) / (Qh + fu_plasma × CLint,scaled); EH = CLh / Qh computed per TKI


Expected output: ivive_results.csv (CLh mL/min/kg + EH per compound) + clearance_summary.json (model assumptions, scaling factors, extraction class flags: Low/Intermediate/High)


Your input CSV has been prepared and is ready to attach to the workflow. Click Run to launch the ivive_hepatic_clearance workflow with the parameters: Qh = 20.7 mL/min/kg, fu_mic = 1.0, model = well-stirred. Extraction ratio flags (EH < 0.3 = Low, 0.3–0.7 = Intermediate, > 0.7 = High) will be annotated automatically in the output.

notes: Expected ordering: Dasatinib(33%) > Bosutinib(9%) > Imatinib(5%) > Nilotinib(0.7%)

ABL1 Kinase Inhibitor Pharmacophore Screening — Builds a consensus pharmacophore from 4 known ABL1 inhibitors and screens a 4-compound library against it using a minimum of 3 matching features.


Input:

Reference SMILES (4 ABL1 inhibitors): Imatinib, Dasatinib, Bosutinib, Asciminib
Library SMILES (4 compounds): Gleevec-analog-1, Ponatinib, Terfenadine, Acetaminophen
min_features: 3



Key steps:

Pharmacophore Model Builder → derives consensus hydrogen-bond acceptor/donor, hydrophobic, and aromatic feature points from the 4 reference SMILES
Feature Matching & Library Screening → scores each library compound against the pharmacophore model, filtering hits by ≥3 matching features
Hit Ranking & Report Generation → outputs ranked hit list with per-compound feature match scores and a visual pharmacophore overlay report



Expected output: pharmacophore_hits.csv (ranked compounds with feature match counts and scores) + pharmacophore_model.json (feature definitions) + HTML screening report showing which library compounds pass the ≥3-feature threshold (expected hits: Gleevec-analog-1 ✓, Ponatinib ✓; expected non-hits: Terfenadine, Acetaminophen)
